Mr. Rajneesh Sharma, Advo  5.
 Mr. Anil Soni, CGSC with   Yadav, Advocate for UOI.
 CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIBHU BAKHRU  HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE TARA VITASTA GANJU  ORDER % 29.05.2024 1.

Learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that the reliance placed by the Respondents on the order dated 10.03.2015 passed by the Supreme Court in Rahul Gupta v. Delhi Development Authority & Ors., SLP 16385-88/2012 is misplaced.

entities.text: Rahul Gupta v. Delhi Development Authority & Ors., SLP 16385-88/2012
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that by a subsequent order dated 28.01.2016, the Court had noted that in that case the physical possession of the subject land was available with DDA for carving into plots for allotment to various allotees.
2. He submits that it is in the said context that the Court had held that it was not possible to accept the legitimacy of the continued possession of the applicants in that case.

3. He points out that the Supreme Court had also held that the said inference would not stand in the way of the Petitioner in his claims under Section 24 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act').

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013

3172/2015, captioned as Balbir Singh & Anr. v. Land Acquisition Collector (North-West) & Anr.,
which was allowed by judgment dated 23.05.2016.

sentences.text: Further, the review petition filed subsequently was also dismissed by the Supreme Court.
4. Thus, decision of the Division Bench of this Court holding that acquisition of the said land had lapsed under Section 24(2) of the Act has attained finality.
5. Learned counsel for the Respondents seek time to examine the aforementioned decisions.

6. List on 21.08.2024.
VIBHU BAKHRU, J TARA VITASTA GANJU, J MAY 29, 2024 pa
